The search turned up a cluster of React hydration-mismatch reports where browser extensions were the likely trigger, though most are closed or unconfirmed.

- **Extensions are a documented cause.** The hydration error text quoted in several issues says a mismatch can happen when a browser extension changes the HTML before React loads (It can also happen if the client has a browser extension installed which messes with the HTML before React loaded.).
- **Video Speed Controller (React 19 RC, Next.js canary).** Issue #31895 reported the error with a Chrome extension, and it was closed as not planned.
- **ColorZilla attribute.** In the Next.js discussion #72035, the reporter traced the mismatch to a cz-shortcut-listen="true" attribute injected by Colorzilla. Disabling the extension fixed it, and a commenter shared a client-side workaround that removes the attribute before hydration.
- **React DevTools script tag.** Issue #25924 (React 18.2.0) describes the script injected by react-devtools chrome extension as a possible cause. It is still marked unconfirmed.
- **Plugin-injected script.** Issue #24430 reports that if a script tag is inserted before the head tag due to the user's browser environment such as a plugin, it is judged as a hydration mismatch. Its resolution is listed as Backlog.
- **Not extension-related.** Issue #36169 (React 19.2.4) reports a hydration error caused by a `<script defer>` inside `<head>` in the app itself, with no extension involved. It is a separate problem that could be confused with extension issues.
- **Adjacent bug.** Issue #33133 (React 19.1.0) concerns `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` combined with `suppressHydrationWarning` and was closed as not planned.

I didn't find an official React fix or a React 19-specific change for extension-injected markup in these results. Versions and states come from the issue pages as they appeared in search, so check each issue for current status.

content.text:
Yes. The closest match to your question is a React 19 report that blames a browser extension, though it was closed without a fix.

**React 19 and extensions**
- [facebook/react #31895](https://github.com/react/react/issues/31895): hydration error with the Video Speed Controller Chrome extension on `next@15.0.4-canary.41` and React `19.0.0-rc`. It was closed as not planned.
- [vercel/next.js Discussion #72035](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/discussions/72035): Next.js 15 with React 19 fails to hydrate because the ColorZilla extension injects `cz-shortcut-listen="true"`. Disabling the extension fixes it, and a commenter shared a client-side workaround.
- [getsentry/sentry-javascript #15886](https://github.com/getsentry/sentry-javascript/issues/15886): about ignoring React 19 hydration errors in Sentry. It is related, but I didn't confirm it names extensions.

**Older extension reports (React 18)**
- [facebook/react #25924](https://github.com/facebook/react/issues/25924): scripts injected by extensions such as React DevTools may cause hydration errors. It is still marked unconfirmed.
- [facebook/react #24430](https://github.com/facebook/react/issues/24430): a plugin-inserted script tag before `<head>` triggers a mismatch. It is in the backlog.

I found no official React fix for extension-injected markup. The usual workarounds are disabling the extension, `suppressHydrationWarning` on the affected element, or removing the injected attributes before hydration. I'm going by the search snippets, not the full issue pages, so check each issue for its current status.
